source.title: Certified Topological Interaction in Neural Representations: Exact Tests and the Statistic They Require

record.tranche_reason: The study measures test performance after memorizing random labels, bearing on V1, and reports generalization-prediction results with different measures from the claim versions.
record.gate_note: The paper's main subject is topological class overlap. E9 measures a random-label-trained model's true-label test accuracy; E5 tests whether overlap summaries predict test accuracy and generalization gap. The other claim versions' specified interventions and measures are not tested.
record.test_reason: E9 extends V1's random-label result to ResNet-20: it fits fixed random CIFAR-10 labels with 0.9999 training accuracy and obtains 0.0995 accuracy on true test labels. The matched natural-label comparison is not reported.
record.authors_conclusion: The record accurately summarizes E9 and E5, but only part of the paper's conclusion. The authors chiefly conclude that scale-free statistics are necessary for their comparative topological tests; class separation is concentrated early in training and in deep layers; and measured higher-order overlap is usually dominated by pairwise overlap. Random-label memorization manufactures this structure in the last stage while true-label test accuracy remains at chance. Raw ECP features predict accuracy but add no predictive value beyond linear probes.
record.recipe_differences: The paper measures representational overlap and generalization prediction rather than the claim versions' interventions or generalization-gap measures; E9 uses a random-label control.
record.method_sensitivity: E9's measured representational effect is confined to the last stage; E5 prediction differs by feature family and is not improved beyond linear-probe baselines.

fits_no_version.finding: E5 reports accuracy-prediction R² of 0.337 for quotient features, 0.935 for raw ECP features, 0.987 for baselines, and 0.841 for total mixup; adding topological features provides no improvement beyond baselines.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Representation-overlap summaries predict held-out accuracy in this population but add no predictive value beyond the tested probe-dominated baselines.

fits_no_version.finding: E11 reports a mean test-accuracy increase of 0.014 when width doubles, without establishing zero training error or convergence.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Doubling ResNet width improves mean CIFAR-10 accuracy under this fixed training recipe.

record.problems: E5 is explicitly exploratory; baseline accuracy prediction is near-ceiling and dominated by linear-probe accuracy. The paper notes dependence among paired statistics and uses assumptions for Benjamini–Hochberg control. The random-label result does not supply the matched natural-label comparison needed for the full V1 claim.
record.rows_left_out: No rows omitted for the 60-row limit. E11 factor contrasts report changes in overlap quotients and overlap mass, not the train–test gap specified by the claim versions; cited prior-work results are not this study's own results.

untested.parts: A matched natural-label run using the random-label architecture and recipe, with natural-label training and held-out accuracy; coexistence under that same recipe.

Test-error behavior beyond the width required for zero training error, trained to convergence without explicit regularization. E11 does not establish that its width contrast crosses or exceeds that threshold.
Convolutional versus fully connected image classifiers and the contribution of local connectivity.
Matched optimizer comparisons and the effects of tuning, decoupled weight decay, or optimizer switching.
Batch-size contrasts under fixed epoch budgets and recipe adaptations.
Dropout interventions, including removal of dropout and weight decay together.
Magnitude-aware weight-perturbation sharpness and its ranking of generalization gaps. Representation overlap is a different measure.
Removing highly memorized examples versus random examples and retraining.

missing.what: A separate random-label training-accuracy row: ResNet-20 reaches 0.9999 after 150 epochs without augmentation or weight decay. This supplies V1's memorization-capacity component; R1 currently records only test accuracy.

record.verdict_notes: The record's limits_scope label mistakes an expected random-label outcome for a limitation. The missing matched natural-label comparison is untested, not contrary evidence. Cross-architecture optimizer differences and overlap changes do not test V4 or V7.

versions.untested_parts: Does not compare the same architecture and recipe trained on natural labels versus random labels for held-out accuracy; does not report natural-label held-out accuracy in this random-label experiment.
